arxiv-1806-06530.title: Segmentation of Photovoltaic Module Cells in Uncalibrated Electroluminescence Images
arxiv-1806-06530.creator: Sergiu Deitsch, Claudia Buerhop-Lutz, Evgenii Sovetkin, Ansgar Steland, Andreas Maier, Florian Gallwitz, Christian Riess
arxiv-1806-06530.description: Abstract High resolution electroluminescence (EL) images captured in the infrared spectrum allow to visually and non-destructively inspect the quality of photovoltaic (PV) modules. Currently, however, such a visual inspection requires trained experts to discern different kinds of defects, which is time-consuming and expensive. Automated segmentation of cells is therefore a key step in automating the visual inspection workflow.

arxiv-2012-07579.title: Energy efficiency of slotted LoRaWAN communication with out-of-band synchronization
arxiv-2012-07579.creator: Luca Beltramelli, Aamir Mahmood, Patrik Österberg, Mikael Gidlund, Paolo Ferrari, and Emiliano Sisinni
arxiv-2012-07579.description: Abstract Although the idea of using wireless links for covering large areas is not new, the advent of Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) has recently started changing the game. Simple, robust, narrowband modulation schemes permit the implementation of low-cost radio devices offering high receiver sensitivity, thus improving the overall link budget.

arxiv-2106-04969.title: Feedback Capacity Formulas of AGN Channels Driven by Nonstationary Autoregressive Moving Average Noise
arxiv-2106-04969.creator: Stelios Louka, Christos Kourtellaris and Charalambos D. Charalambous
arxiv-2106-04969.description: Abstract In this paper we derive closed-form formulas of feedback capacity and nonfeedback achievable rates, for Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN) channels driven by nonstationary autoregressive moving average (ARMA) noise (with unstable one poles and zeros), based on time-invariant feedback codes and channel input distributions.

arxiv-2111-09791.title: Supporting Undotted Arabic with Pre-trained Language Models
arxiv-2111-09791.creator: Aviad Rom, Kfir Bar
arxiv-2111-09791.description: Abstract We observe a recent behaviour on social media, in which users intentionally remove consonantal dots from Arabic letters, in order to bypass content-classification algorithms. Content classification is typically done by fine-tuning pre-trained language models, which have been recently employed by many natural-language-processing applications.

arxiv-2207-06598.title: Formation of Quiescent Prominence Magnetic Field by Supergranulations Journal: ApJL MPI-AMRVAC, PDFI_SS
arxiv-2207-06598.creator: Qingjun Liu, Chun Xia
arxiv-2207-06598.description: Abstract To understand the formation of quiescent solar prominences, the origin of their magnetic field structures, i.e., magnetic flux ropes (MFRs), must be revealed. We use three-dimensional magnetofriction simulations in a spherical subdomain to investigate the role of typical supergranular motions in the long-term formation of a prominence magnetic field.

arxiv-2301-03864.title: MeerKAT discovery of 13 new pulsars in Omega Centauri 2015 MeerKAT discovery of 13 new pulsars in Omega Centauri –
arxiv-2301-03864.creator: W. Chen, P. C. C. Freire, A. Ridolfi, E. D. Barr, B. Stappers, M. Kramer, A. Possenti, S. M. Ransom, L. Levin, R. P. Breton, M. Burgay, F. Camilo, S. Buchner, D. J. Champion, F. Abbate, V. Venkatraman Krishnan, P. V. Padmanabh, T. Gautam, L. Vleeschower, M. Geyer, J-M. Grießmeier, Y. P. Men, V. Bala
arxiv-2301-03864.description: Abstract The most massive globular cluster in our Galaxy, Omega Centauri, is an interesting target for pulsar searches, because of its multiple stellar populations and the intriguing possibility that it was once the nucleus of a galaxy that was absorbed into the Milky Way.

arxiv-2312-09400.title: Refuting approaches to the log-rank conjecture for XOR functions
arxiv-2312-09400.creator: Hamed Hatami, Kaave Hosseini, Shachar Lovett, Anthony Ostuni
arxiv-2312-09400.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hamed Hatami, Kaave Hosseini, Shachar Lovett, Anthony Ostuni. The log-rank conjecture, a longstanding problem in communication complexity, has persistently eluded resolution for decades. Consequently, some recent efforts have focused on potential approaches for establishing the conjecture in the special case of XOR functions, where the communication matrix is lifted from a boolean function, and the rank of the matrix equals the Fourier sparsity of the function, which is the number of its nonzero Fourier coefficients. In this note, we refute two conjectures.

arxiv-2312-10169.title: Review of Unsupervised POS Tagging and Its Implications on Language Acquisition
arxiv-2312-10169.description: Abstract An ability that underlies human syntactic knowledge is determining which words can appear in the similar structures (i.e. grouping words by their syntactic categories). These groupings enable humans to combine structures in order to communicate complex meanings. A foundational question is how do children acquire this ability underlying syntactic knowledge.

arxiv-2503-10284.title: PyGDA: A Python Library for Graph Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2503-10284.creator: Zhen Zhang zhen@nus.edu.sg, Meihan Liu lmh_zju@zju.edu.cn, Bingsheng He hebs@comp.nus.edu.sg
arxiv-2503-10284.description: Abstract Graph domain adaptation has emerged as a promising approach to facilitate knowledge transfer across different domains. Recently, numerous models have been proposed to enhance their generalization capabilities in this field. However, there is still no unified library that brings together existing techniques and simplifies their implementation.

arxiv-2505-15803.title: Adaptive Estimation and Learning under Temporal Distribution Shift
arxiv-2505-15803.creator: Dheeraj Baby, Yifei Tang, Hieu Duy Nguyen, Yu-Xiang Wang, Rohit Pyati
arxiv-2505-15803.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the problem of estimation and learning under temporal distribution shift. Consider an observation sequence of length n n , which is a noisy realization of a time-varying groundtruth sequence. Our focus is to develop methods to estimate the groundtruth at the final time-step while providing sharp point-wise estimation error rates.

arxiv-2507-02382.title: Interval-sphere model structures
arxiv-2507-02382.creator: Kathryn Hess, Samuel Lavenir, Kelly Maggs
arxiv-2507-02382.description: Abstract . The bedrock of persistence theory over a single parameter is decomposition of persistence modules into intervals. In [ HLM24 ] , the authors leveraged interval decomposition to produce a cell decomposition of the minimal model of a simply connected copersistent space.

arxiv-2507-11377.title: Moving Beyond Marginal Carbon Intensity
arxiv-2507-11377.creator: Philipp Wiesner Technische Universität Berlin wiesner@tu-berlin.de, Odej Kao Technische Universität Berlin odej.kao@tu-berlin.de
arxiv-2507-11377.description: Abstract Marginal Carbon Intensity (MCI) has been promoted as an effective metric for carbon-aware computing. Although it is already considered as impractical for carbon accounting purposes, many still view it as valuable when optimizing for grid flexibility by incentivizing electricity usage during curtailment periods. In this statement paper, we argue that MCI is neither reliable nor actionable for either purpose.

pmc-11540898.title: Assessing the Utility of the DAPT Score and PRECISE-DAPT Score in Determining the Appropriateness of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction/Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
pmc-11540898.creator: Abhishek Singh, M. A. Hussain, Shyam Chand Chaudhary, Akriti Bharadwaj, K. K. Sawalani, Akshyaya Pradhan, Rishi Sethi
pmc-11540898.description: Background: Utilizing the two available prediction models, i.e., the dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) score and predicting bleeding complication in patients undergoing stent implantation and subsequent dual antiplatelet therapy (PRECISE-DAPT) score, we aimed to determine the appropriateness of the DAPT in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

pmc-11860842.title: Exploring psychological distress among psychiatric nurses in Tunisia
pmc-11860842.creator: H Khiari, A Hakiri, M Bouchendira, R Ghachem
pmc-11860842.description: IntroductionNurses working in psychiatric departments regularly encounter intricate, stress-inducing, and emotionally challenging situations. The mental well-being of these nurses directly influences the quality of care they deliver.ObjectivesTo assess the prevalence of psychological distress among psychiatric nurses and to identify the socio-demographic and clinical factors associated with it.

pmc-13126571.title: From MDGs experience to SDGs Actions: Insights from Tanzanian Nurses and Midwives
pmc-13126571.creator: Peter Taratara, Elaine Bennett, Selma Alliex
pmc-13126571.description: Background:Nurses and midwives constitute the largest proportion of the health workforce and play a central role in achieving maternal and child health outcomes. During the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) era, particularly MDGs 4 and 5, their engagement was considered essential.

pmc-13374408.title: Architecture, implementation and acceptance of performance-based resource allocation for medical education: an interview study protocol addressing medical schools in Germany and Switzerland
pmc-13374408.creator: Marc Ninck, Yara Banz, Sissel Guttormsen
pmc-13374408.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionPerformance-based resource allocation (PBRA) programmes have been increasingly adopted by medical schools as a strategic mechanism to optimise funding distribution, align resources with institutional priorities—particularly the delivery of high-quality education—and improve educational outcomes. In an era of budgetary constraints and growing demands for transparency and accountability in higher education, PBRA programmes offer means to enhance efficiency, incentivise quality and strengthen educational performance. Despite their widespread implementation, significant knowledge gaps remain.

pmc-13505918.creator: Laura Ceballos, Candela Canton, Valeria Gayo, Laura Moreno, Carlos Lanusse, Luis Alvarez
pmc-13505918.description: Although oxfendazole (OFZ) has been traditionally used to control nematode parasites in domestic animals and more recently in human medicine, high efficacy against porcine cysticercosis and fasciolosis in both sheep and pigs has been observed when the drug is administered at higher dose levels.

pmc-13586788.title: Cone‐Beam Computed Tomography–Derived Alveolar Anatomy for Immediate Implant Planning: Thickness, Concavity, and Angulation Patterns: A Comprehensive Evaluation

pmc-13711445.title: Marked Underreferral to Structural Heart Specialists in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation Despite High Clinical Burden: An Adjusted Registry Analysis
pmc-13711445.creator: Prince Darko, John Costner, Brennan Carter, Baffour Otchere, Christopher Chinnatambi, Papa Beeko, Patrick Berchie, Oladipo Odeyinka, Eunice Hama, Swethapriya Chaparala

The primary outcome was the absence of structural heart disease (SHD) specialist evaluation.
